flags.issue: UNDECIDABLE: The only deterministic non-AI evaluation in QCT's loop is the build step — QCT runs `mvn clean compile` and iterates over compiler/build errors to fix the migrated code (Sec. 3; migration Steps 1–5 show javac/Maven errors like 'package org.junit.runner does not exist' driving fixes). This is a deterministic type/syntax checker used inside the system, which half-fits the 'type checkers' fires-on list, but a plain build-and-fix compile loop reads more like build orchestration than a purpose-built rule-based analyser (no linter/SAST/security-scanner/formal verifier is described; QCT is an external commercial tool whose internals are not detailed; P8's wish for a 'list of security checks' is conjecture, not an implemented check). Flagging rather than emitting per default-to-silence.

TESTS: unit tests (junit) run by QCT as part of the migration/upgrade validation ('conducting unit tests, and verifying deployment readiness', Sec. 3; junit dependency added in migration Step 4; participants in Sec. 5.2.2 treat passing tests as the key trust signal); AUTHOR: human — the study migrates existing open-source Java repositories whose test suites were written by their original human developers, while the migrated code is model-generated by QCT.
